neighbours.label: the slot right before '(just) a few' in the list-closing idiom 'to name / mention / list (just) a few'; 'name' elsewhere and other list endings stay quiet
fire: The market stalls sell honey, olives and figs, to name a few.
She has lived in Lagos, Lima and Lyon, just to name a few.
The app supports Spanish, Hindi and Korean, to name just a few.
Guests included poets, chefs and architects, to name but a few.
Common allergens are nuts, eggs and shellfish, to mention a few.
He plays guitar, banjo and mandolin, just to name a few.
The museum holds works by Goya, Turner and Klee, to name only a few.
Side effects such as nausea, dizziness and fatigue, to list a few, were reported.
quiet: The market stalls sell honey, olives and figs, among other things.
She has lived in Lagos, Lima and Lyon, and a few smaller towns.
The app supports Spanish, Hindi and Korean, and more are coming.
Guests were asked to write their name in the visitors' book.
Common allergens are nuts, eggs and shellfish, the doctor explained.
The parents could not agree on what to name the puppy.
The museum holds works by Goya, Turner and Klee, and so on.
Only a few side effects, such as nausea, were reported.

notes: Probes: to name a few 0.64, to list just a few 0.56, to mention a few 0.48, to name but a few 0.46; 'write your name' 0.09, 'among other things' 0.11. It also fires on the minutes of a clock time (10:30 a.m. or p.m., 9:15 in the morning: 0.37-0.48), which this label does not cover, so the near misses contain no clock times.
